title: Two tiers on two hosts run at the same time
description:
The point of the feature: low on OpenCode, mid on Codex, high on Claude Code, all burning under one `dispatch.concurrency`. Nothing in core should assume one host per board any more.

One integration test proves it: two ready nodes scored to two tiers, `dispatch.tiers` pointing at two of the fake hosts in test/integration/hosts, `sober run a b`. Both start, both run records name their own host, each log renders through its own adapter (`renderLine` in hosts.ts already picks by event shape), and `--watch` on the Codex-tier node is refused by tier while the Claude-tier node is attended. The same pair started by the unattended queue (packages/core/src/queue.ts, ADR 0056) resolves the host per node, not once for the batch.

Fix whatever the test finds that assumes a single host — the batch probe, the per-run host string, anything keyed by `config.dispatch.host`. No new surface; this node is the test and the fixes it forces.
